architecture.mechanism: Real-time estimation of electromagnetic torque and d-q axis stator reactance via a moving-average-filtered third-order generalized integrator flux observer, feeding an adaptive predictive model that is updated each sampling instant and enforces current constraints, so operating-point-dependent nonlinearities (inductance variation, flux weakening) are tracked rather than mis-modeled.
architecture.intervention: Embed the filtered third-order generalized integrator flux observer in the rear motor inverter's control software to continuously estimate torque and stator reactance; use the adaptive linear MPC's current-constraint enforcement and per-sample model update to detect inverter/motor operating-point drift early, then command a controlled torque derate plus a "pull over safely" warning instead of allowing a hard shutdown.
architecture.expected_effect: Incipient inverter failure signatures (reactance/inductance variation, flux weakening, current imbalance) are detected while propulsion is still available, so the warning is issued with residual torque authority maintained, giving the driver the 10-15 seconds needed to reach a safe pullover spot before total power loss.
architecture.falsification_test: On a vehicle or HIL bench, inject a representative rear inverter fault (phase open/short, gate-driver loss, capacitor degradation) and log (a) time from fault onset to driver warning and (b) time from warning to total propulsion loss; the mechanism is falsified if warning-to-loss is under 10-15 s or if the observer's torque/reactance estimates show no detectable deviation before catastrophic shutdown.
